trajectory_summary: The agent populated a provided Excel template (test-rar.xlsx) via openpyxl: it copied monthly gold prices from /root/data/gold-prices.xlsx into the “Gold price” sheet, added formulas for log returns and rolling volatilities, then filled the “Answer” sheet for STEP 1 (C3:C6), STEP 2 (country list, 2023 gold values including Sweden conversion from Volume, and exposure formulas), and STEP 3 (replicated STEP 2, pulled 2023 total reserves via INDEX/MATCH, and computed RaR%). The agent attempted to run LibreOffice-based recalculation (/skills/xlsx/recalc.py) but it repeatedly errored (“list index out of range”) and produced workbooks that openpyxl could not load due to stylesheet/named-style index errors (turns 31–37). It then regenerated and saved a clean /root/output/rar_result.xlsx without recalculation (turn 39) and confirmed formulas were present (turn 40). Official feedback shows many key numeric items failed (notably STEP 1 volatilities, STEP 2 exposures, and STEP 3 RaR%), indicating the final spreadsheet did not meet task requirements despite being saved successfully.
what_worked: Gold prices were populated into the template’s “Gold price” sheet (turn 40 shows numeric prices in column B for 2022M9–2023M9, e.g., row 14 includes 1915.434761904762).
Monthly log return formulas (LN ratio * 100) were inserted in “Gold price” column C (turn 40: row 3 formula '=IF(OR(B3="",B2=""),"",LN(B3/B2)*100)').

STEP 2 country list and 2023 gold value links were filled (turn 40 row 11 C–K: ['Austria', ..., 'Sweden']; row 12 includes '=Value!C18' etc., and Sweden conversion via Volume*AVERAGEIF). This aligns with official feedback showing multiple step2:*:gold_value tests passed.

STEP 3 total reserves lookup formulas were created using INDEX/MATCH (turn 40 row 23 formulas like '=IFERROR(INDEX(...MATCH("2023",...),MATCH(C20&':*',...)),"")'), matching official feedback where step3:*:total_reserves tests passed.

The final output file was written to the required location and preserved (turn 41 shows only /root/output/rar_result.xlsx remains; turn 39 prints 'saved /root/output/rar_result.xlsx' and 'reopen ok').

issues.where: turn 39–40 (Gold price volatility formulas; Answer STEP 1)
issues.evidence: Volatility formulas were built with STDEV.P (turn 40: 'Gold price'!D5 contains '...STDEV.P(C3:C5)' and E14 contains '...STDEV.P(C3:C14)'). Answer STEP 1 pulls these via LOOKUP (turn 40: C4 '=LOOKUP(...,''Gold price''!D:D)', C6 '=LOOKUP(...,''Gold price''!E:E)'). Official feedback reports step1:C4, step1:C5, and step1:C6 all failed.
issues.cause: The volatility definition/annualization did not match what the benchmark expects (likely sample vs population standard deviation and/or expected annualization conventions), producing incorrect STEP 1 outputs and contaminating downstream risk calculations.

issues.evidence: Exposure formulas were set to 'value*$C$3*($C$4/100)*SQRT(3)' (turn 40 row 13 C–K). RaR% formulas were set to 'exposure/total_reserves*100' (turn 40 row 24 C–K). Official feedback shows all step2:*:exposure tests failed and all step3:*:rar_percent tests failed.
issues.cause: Exposure/RaR depended on the (failed) STEP 1 volatility outputs and may also reflect a mismatch in expected horizon-scaling/volatility input (e.g., which volatility measure to use and whether it is already annualized), resulting in systematic errors across all countries.

issues.evidence: Recalculation attempts failed: turn 31 '/skills/xlsx/recalc.py /root/output/rar_result.xlsx' returned '{ "error": "list index out of range" }'. After this, openpyxl could not load the workbook due to stylesheet named-style expansion errors (turn 35–36 traceback: IndexError in 'stylesheet._expand_named_style'). Even running recalc.py on a fresh template copy failed (turn 37).
issues.cause: The LibreOffice-based recalc pipeline appears incompatible with the workbook’s style/named-style structures, leading to failures/corruption and preventing the agent from recalculating/validating numeric results inside the spreadsheet during debugging.

outcome_rationale: Official feedback shows only 24/43 checks passed, with critical outputs (STEP 1 volatility cells, STEP 2 exposures, STEP 3 RaR%) failing, so the saved /root/output/rar_result.xlsx is very likely incorrect for the task.
